To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the demand for cost accounting information on the railway was a response to the desire of the government to regulate the industry, that the demand for accounting data was not a response to the need for information for internal management purposes and that the demand for this type of information was not a response by the railway companies to the desire to improve efficiency.
The development of cost information was a consequence of the desire to regulate the railway industry.
the demand for accounting information on Britain's rail network was stimulated by the desire to co‐ordinate the transport undertakings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of management accounting systems on Britain's railways from the 1930s to the 1950s.
the analysis of management information in an ‘accounting’ format.
the development of accounting in the context of the public sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of cost accounting on Britain's railways is a direct result of regulation.
accounting information has developed on Britain's rail network as a result of government intervention, and not as a result of the market.
the development of accounting information on the railways was the result of government regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
accounting information has been developed to meet the demands of regulation and, as such, the development of management information on British railways was a product of regulation.
the accounting information that was developed was a reflection of the political and regulatory context in which the railway operated.
we have shown that there is a relationship between the demand for management accounting data, the political and economic environment and the development of accounting information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the demand for management accounting information is not always a result of the internal pressures of an organisation.
the development of management accounting information was not simply an internal matter but was shaped by the wider political and economic environment.
the demand for accounting information can develop in the absence of a market‐based economy.
